svg.title: Original rules
svg.desc: Original rules: seven steps of one dungeon trip. Each box is what the game does; each speech bubble is what the player is thinking. The same text is in the README.

g.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
g.text: Original rules
Original mode, or extra content with the five ARRANGE switches Off
What the game does
What the player is thinking
You enter the dungeon.
HP is full, the SUP.HP / SUP.TP pools are full (your refill
reserve), the bag holds 12 heals.
“The pools are my budget for this whole
trip. Every point I spend comes out of
them.”
Fight 1, three weak enemies.
You take 300 damage. After the win, HP stays where it is. If
you switched on the game's own Auto Fill option, HP refills
and the SUP.HP pool pays for it 1:1 (Auto Fill is off at new
game in Original mode; on in extra-content mode).
“Fine, cheap fight. Refill now from the
pool, or carry the damage and save the
pool? Pool first, it is early.”
Fight 2, a tougher pair.
One enemy inflicts Slow. You weigh curing it or hitting
harder.
“If I cure, that is an action lost. If I
ignore it, I take two more hits. Cure, the
boss is still ahead.”
Fight 3, an ambush.
You try to escape. The roll fails. You take a round of
damage, then it works.
“Escape is a dice roll. Burned a turn
and 400 HP. The pool will not cover the
boss if this keeps up.”
Between fights.
The pool is at 30 percent. You check the bag.
This is the decision the original game is built around.
“Use heals now, or save them for the
boss? Turn back to the save tree and
refill the pools, or push on?”
Boss.
HP starts wherever you left it. You can throw as many heals
as you own. The boss shrugs off your ailment spells; your
counterattack sphere triggers now and then, on its roll.
“Ailments won't stick on him. It comes
down to his elemental weakness, my
stats and my heal count. Spam heals,
outlast, keep everyone alive.”
After the boss.
Pools nearly empty, bag half gone.
“Back to a save tree before the next
area. I need the refill.”
